questions.trap_note: COUNT(*) counts ROWS (including the one with a NULL amount); COUNT(amount) skips NULLs. The obvious COUNT(*) gives 5 — wrong.
questions.prompt: Return how many orders have an amount actually recorded (i.e. not missing).
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer TEXT, amount INT);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES
  (1, 'asha', 250),
  (2, 'vikram', 120),
  (3, 'asha', NULL),
  (4, 'meena', 400),
  (5, 'vikram', 90);
questions.explain: COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values in that column — 4 here. COUNT(*) counts rows — 5. The seed data plants exactly one NULL so the wrong query is visibly wrong, not accidentally right.

questions.prompt: A filter on an aggregate (e.g. keep only customers whose SUM(amount) exceeds 300) cannot go in WHERE — it belongs in the ______ clause.
questions.answer: HAVING — WHERE filters individual rows BEFORE grouping (aggregates don't exist yet); HAVING filters groups AFTER GROUP BY has computed the aggregates.
questions.explain: Order of operations: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY. WHERE runs before groups exist, so SUM() in WHERE is an error; HAVING runs on the grouped result.

questions.prompt: Return each customer's total order value (customer, total), highest total first. Treat missing amounts as 0.
questions.schema_sql:
CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer TEXT, amount INT);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES
  (1, 'asha', 250),
  (2, 'vikram', 120),
  (3, 'asha', NULL),
  (4, 'meena', 400),
  (5, 'vikram', 90);
questions.canonical_query: SELECT customer, SUM(COALESCE(amount, 0)) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer ORDER BY total DESC;
questions.explain: GROUP BY collapses rows per customer; COALESCE turns the NULL into 0 (plain SUM would silently skip it — same totals here, but the habit matters when a whole group is NULL); ORDER BY total DESC ranks them: meena 400, asha 250, vikram 210.
